text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - perf cliff detected in continuous-batching runtime (svc: inference-gateway) at 20:14 UTC. High concurrency, queueing growing, P95 tokens latency spike. Autoretry rate increasing. https://grafana/redwood/dashboard/abcd

alice: seeing it too, queue depth up on multiple hosts, KV cache hit-rate collapsed from 98% to 11% in last 90s.

bob: logs show huge prefetch bursts: repeated `prefetch_request` flood and KV write errors, disk-backed spillback observed on node-7.

carla: customer impact? any 500s or just latency?

alice: primarily latency > 5s on chat generation, a tiny % of 5xx (timeout on backend inference). A few timeouts from long-running microbatches.

devon: looks like microbatch size oscillation — microbatch target jumped due to jitter estimator. microbatch sizes 64 -> 1024 repeatedly. That blows through KV mem working set.

tina: confirming, autoscaler metrics show many inflight requests stuck waiting in continuous batch queue. Throughput down 30% for p99-sensitive routes.

bob: I'm going to pin batching config to safe defaults. Will push hotfix: set CB_MAX_MICROBATCH=128, PREFETCH_WINDOW=0.7, KV_WRITE_RATE_LIMIT=5000.

alice: 👍 do we need to failover to older model variant temporarily? Might be faster than immediate patch.

carla: Ops ask — any customer-facing outage? Support ticket queue shows elevated latency complaints for 3 customers (enterprise). No broad outage yet.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: deploy id d-7824 by bob -> staging -> prod canary.

bob: deploying hotfix to canary now. Command:
```
redwoodctl deploy --service inference-gateway --env prod --set CB_MAX_MICROBATCH=128 --set PREFETCH_WINDOW=0.7 --set KV_WRITE_RATE_LIMIT=5000 --canary 5%
```

devon: rolling canary good so far on 5% hosts, KV hit-rate recovering to ~60% on those nodes. Queue depth dropping.

alice: start canary traffic steering to previously affected routes, watch p95 and queue length.

carla: notifying support to message impacted customers: "We're aware of elevated latency; mitigation in progress, tracking with engineering."

bob: promoting to 25% -> 100% after 3m stable.

deploy-bot: canary promoting: 25% -> 100%.

bob: full rollout done. KV hit-rate across fleet back to 95% in 6 minutes. P95 latency trending down to baseline.

devon: follow-up: root cause appears to be a recent jitter estimator tweak (PR #5123) that over-estimated batching window under heavy concurrency, causing microbatches to grow and prefetch to overshoot. Prefetch + big microbatches overwhelmed KV cache eviction heuristics.

alice: good catch. Action items:
- bob: revert or patch jitter estimator to avoid runaway growth (owner)
- devon: add a circuit breaker to cap microbatch growth under high concurrency and fallback to fixed microbatch size (owner)
- tina: run a perf replay test with synthetic high-concurrency traffic to validate (owner)
- carla: customer coms draft and postmortem prep (owner)

carla: I'll open a support note and schedule postmortem meeting 1hr. Draft message: "We mitigated an elevated latency incident caused by batching/prefetch interactions; engineering applied a config hotfix. We'll follow up with technical details and actions."

alice: marking incident as acknowledged. Paging quieted. If anyone sees re-escalation, ping here.

bob: PR for jitter estimator change reverted: https://stash/redwood/PR/5177. Will open a follow-up with safer backoff logic.

devon: adding telemetry: new gauge for microbatch_size_percentile and a runaway counter that triggers autoscaler backoff if microbatch growth > 3x baseline in 30s.

tina: running stress replay now, will report results in 20m.

carla: thanks all. High-priority postmortem scheduled. Support already emailed the 3 affected customers.

alice: closing pager thread for now, leaving this thread as handoff for postmortem writers.

bob: note for postmortem: include timeline, diffs of config changes, canary graphs (kv hit, p95, queue depth), and the deploy id.

incident-bot: Incident closed (auto): all alerts cleared, runbook step completed.
